summary: NASA's 3D model of the Space Launch System, cut into its pieces by its profile, colored as it flew on Artemis I, staging in the flight's order, much faster than real.

claims.claim: The pieces separate in the order of Artemis I: the two boosters, the launch abort system, the core stage, then Orion leaves the upper stage (the ICPS).
claims.how: The drive moves each piece at its time on a 12-second clock; the test checks the order and that the boosters fall away to both sides, tilting outward.

sources.title: Space Launch System Solid Rocket Booster
sources.says: After launch, the boosters operate for about two minutes before separating from the core stage and landing in the Atlantic Ocean.

sources.title: Artemis I
sources.says: The Orion spacecraft and ICPS were both placed into a nominal orbit after separating from the Space Launch System, achieving orbit approximately 8 1/2 minutes after launch. Eighty-nine minutes after liftoff, the ICPS fired for approximately eighteen minutes in a trans-lunar injection (TLI) maneuver. Orion then separated from the expended stage.

claims.note: The abort system's jettison comes after the boosters' separation, as on every SLS flight; its exact time is not given in these sources.

claims.claim: The core stage is orange and the boosters, upper stage and Orion white, as on Artemis I.
claims.how: tools/sp2-rockets.mjs colors the model's pieces (the printable model has no color).
claims.note: From NASA photographs of Artemis I on the pad and in flight (orange foam on the core stage, white boosters and fairings); no text source quoted. The shades are chosen by eye.

claims.claim: The model is NASA's, used under NASA's media guidelines, and carries no logo.
claims.how: The printable model is one untextured solid; the test checks the GLB has no image or texture.

sources.title: Images and media usage guidelines
sources.says: NASA content (images, audio, video, and computer files used in the rendition of 3-dimensional models...) generally are not subject to copyright in the United States.

simplified: Staging that took hours is shown in 12 seconds.
The flames are glowing cones, not a simulation of the exhaust.
Orion's crew module, hidden under the abort system's fairing in the model, is drawn as a plain cone.
The model is simplified to about 48,000 triangles.
